description.value: Built in 1911 by Captain Henry Pybus, St Clair Hotel-Hostel is one of Vancouver's oldest heritage buildings and the city's first concrete structure, originally designed to welcome travelers arriving by train and ship. It operates today as a nautical-themed hostel in downtown Vancouver, offering private rooms across several configurations — single, double, twin, triple, and family quad — with shared washrooms and a kitchenette. Located steps from SkyTrain, beaches, parks, and city attractions, it caters to budget-conscious travelers seeking private accommodation in the urban core.
